content: S2 one view: the server forwards the rows a session may work to that session's client (the BusEvent::TodoUpdated the server folds into the member cache today, server.rs:2065), and the client renders one surface from it, absorbing the inline card, the side-panel page, the pinned band, the info pips and the gallery's at-a-glance role. Deletes four renderers, four caches and fifteen file reads. Gate: the four old surfaces gone; a live TUI check on a run with two workers showing progress, holder and status; the client suite.
note: The code half is whole in four children: t26 3ef4a4c5, t27 d867fee8, t28 d84a627f, t29 5ea5618d (-6,384 lines). One read (server), one model (pushed rows), one surface (the pinned list; card, page, pips and roster gone). Remaining gate: the live TUI smoke test on a run with two workers, in docs/plans/task-flow.md under S2. Close this row when that passes; then S3 (t16) unblocks.

content: S3 one status (waits on S2): liveness becomes the holder's own session status plus one predicate for a holder that can never return; delete SwarmMemberRuntime.todo_items (the third copy of a session's rows), the four member shapes and the third event log. Gate: the member cache gone, one predicate decides liveness, the TUI reads the typed status.

S5 status, priority and group leave TaskItem, with the four status vocabularies they keep alive (kcode-plan's five helpers, kcode-base's canonical_todo_status and its wrappers, the TUI's normalize_plan_status_for_todo, status_badge and the second priority_rank). Afterwards readiness is blocked_by empty and liveness comes from the member, not the item. Gate: the three fields gone and the vocabularies with them.

D2 the swarm/comm condense: the SwarmState handle pair is rebuilt as a literal at each request arm and threaded to ~40 functions; give the swarm state its one owner and delete the pair. This is the work that gates plans/server-shape.md H2. Gate: no SwarmState literal at a request arm.
G1 restore the two size ratchets in scripts/check_guardrails.sh and re-baseline both with --update; they are paused with the reason at the call site.

G2 the one live kcode run probe against its own socket, in a scratch repo, run by the user: the permission (a granted turn continues, a wake does not) and the poke's removal (no client continuation; every non-retryable error gets the short budget). It is the lane's landing proof, so it runs when the list is done, not per step.

note: S4 (t17) and G3 (t24) landed 2026-10-04. S2 (t15) is the gate; S3 waits on it and S5 waits on S3 (compiler-proven). D2's gate is already satisfied but the pair threading is ~100 sites. Needs a maintainer call before the TUI reshape.
